rounds.text: Lee & Nee Software (Exports) Ltd is currently positioned for a potential turnaround, evidenced by a consistent long-term trajectory of 18% compounded sales growth over the last decade [E14] and a notable recent surge in performance, including 40% YoY sales growth and 87% YoY net profit growth [E55, E57]. The company is fundamentally robust with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E37] and a strong current ratio of 6.22x, ensuring comfortable short-term liquidity [E38]. Management confidence is reflected in the increasing promoter stake, which rose to 70.18% as of September 2026 [E41]. Furthermore, the company is actively improving its operational efficiency, with the yearly operating margin trend showing consistent improvement over the last five years [E32] and a 10 percentage point increase in the TTM operating margin compared to three years ago [E30]. While the stock trades at a discount to its book value at 0.68x [E2, E50], it is currently outperforming market expectations as profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 39% [E47]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E34, E35], a high P/E ratio [E1, E6], and low return on equity [E9, E13, E52].

Compounded profit growth over 5 years sits at -5%, and 3-year share price growth has dropped by -3%, showing that long-term fundamental wealth creation is failing to support the valuation [E19, E24]. Operating cash flow and free cash flow both turned negative in March 2026 at Rs -1.11 Cr and Rs -1.38 Cr respectively, driving a dreadful cash conversion ratio of -3.58x against reported profit [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, debtor days have stretched upward from 27.0 to 42.1 days, reflecting deteriorating working capital quality [E53]. A discounted cash flow model calculates a massive overvaluation with a negative margin of safety of -825.0%, meaning the current share price of Rs 6.96 rests on extreme, unsupported expectations of 30.0% future earnings growth [E43, E44, E45]. conceded: [E30]

The bear highlights a 5-year compounded profit decline of -5% and a 3-year share price drop of -3% [E19, E24], but ignores the powerful accelerating top-line momentum featuring 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year compounded sales growths of 18%, 17%, and respectively 20% [E14, E15, E16], alongside recent massive surges of +40% YoY sales and +87% to +88% YoY net profit growth [E55, E57, E63]. While negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -1.11 Cr and Rs -1.38 Cr in March 2026 are present [E35, E36], conceded: [E34], the business is almost entirely debt-free with a pristine 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio and comfortable short-term liquidity boasting a 6.22x current ratio [E37, E38, E49]. The claim of stretched working capital via debtor days rising to 42.1 days [E53] is counterbalanced by an impressive operational turnaround where operating margins have expanded by +10 percentage points over three years and +5 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E30, E31], driving an exceptional results score of 86/100 that outperforms stale sentiment [E63]. Finally, pointing to a negative DCF margin of safety [E43, E44] completely misses the deeply discounted tangible backing of a price-to-book ratio at just 0.68x against a book value of ₹ 10.3 [E2], while committed insiders have actively increased their stake to 70.18% [E41].

While the bull cites accelerating sales growth of 18%, 17%, and 20% over 10, 5, and 3 years [E14, E15, E16], this top-line expansion fails to translate into durable shareholder returns, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit decline of -5% [E19], a 3-year share price drop of -3% [E24], and a miserable median return on equity of 0% to 1% across 10, 5, 3, and 1-year horizons [E26, E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: the business maintains a 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio, a 6.22x current ratio [E37, E38], and a 70.18% promoter stake [E41], but these defensive balance sheet metrics sit alongside deteriorating cash health, including a negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.11 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -1.38 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. The bull highlights margin expansion and a strong recent results score [E30, E31, E63], yet debtor days have simultaneously worsened from 27.0 to 42.1 days [E53], amplifying working capital strain. Furthermore, dismissing the DCF valuation warning of -825% [E43, E44, E61] by pointing to a 0.68x P/B ratio [E2] ignores the reality that the stock trades at an inflated P/E of 97.5x [E1] or 105x against sector benchmarks [E6], while paying a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and relying on a reverse DCF that already demands an aggressive 30.0% earnings growth rate from the current price [E45].
